name: Pelatiah
overview: Pelatiah was a male member of the tribe of Simeon, identified specifically as the son of Ishi. His mention in Scripture highlights his lineage within the Simeonite community, reflecting the genealogical records important to the biblical narrative. Beyond this, no additional notes provide further detail about his life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Pelatiah means 'YHWH rescues,' indicating a theologically rich meaning that underscores God's saving power. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:42, was not given by God directly but carries a significant reminder of divine deliverance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Pelatiah was the son of Ishi, as noted in 1 Chronicles 4:42. No other family relationships are detailed beyond this connection within the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Pelatiah's significance lies primarily in his place within the genealogical record of the tribe of Simeon. His identification as the son of Ishi situates him within the broader narrative of Israel's tribal history, emphasizing the continuity of God's chosen people. While not a central figure in biblical events, his mention preserves the heritage and identity of Simeonite descendants.
